content:
maria (customer): hey team — starting ~09:10 UTC we started getting a bunch of 502/504 timeouts from the /v1/generate endpoint. ~30% of calls failing, latencies spiking to 15–25s before a gateway timeout. our app started returning errors to users.

sarah (support): hey @maria — sorry about that. can you paste the request id(s) and the org id? any chance you saw an auth/403 message or a billing notice in the portal?

maria (customer): org: org_42abc. request ids: req_9a8b7c, req_9a8b7d. we DID see some 429s earlier but not 403s. billing email showed a failed payment at 08:55 but its marked resolved now.

ryan (oncall): I'm seeing a matching surge in hosted-prod gateway metrics and a lot of "upstream timed out" from gateway. traces show a long queue time before reaching model pods. timeline: ~09:08 backpressure + 09:10 first 504s.

ashish (eng-sre): digging into autoscaling metrics. KEDA scaledObject for that model group isn't creating new replicas quickly — polling interval is the default 30s and cooldown is 300s. Also seeing errors from keda-operator logs: "failed to get external metric: metrics.k8s.io not available" which explains why it couldn't trigger HPA.

ben (eng-runtime): runtime logs from model-pool show slow model loads on cold start: "model load time=11.7s, weights read=9.8s" per pod. combined with readinessProbe configured with low initialDelay means pods aren't marked ready fast enough for traffic to route, so gateway queues and then times out.

ashish (eng-sre): here's the scaledobject snippet we found (sanitized):
```yaml
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
metadata:
  name: model-group-scaledobj
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    name: model-pool-deploy
  pollingInterval: 30
  cooldownPeriod: 300
  minReplicaCount: 0
  maxReplicaCount: 10
  triggers:
  - type: prometheus
    metadata:
      serverAddress: http://prometheus.monitoring.svc
      metricName: model_queue_length
      threshold: "50"
```

ashish (eng-sre): with minReplicaCount=0 and long cooldown, the first burst pays cold start tax + KEDA poll delay. also KEDA couldn't read metrics intermittently because metrics-server was flakey for a short window — see keda-operator logs: "error listing external metrics: Get \"/apis/external.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1\": 503"

sarah (support): @ryan can we confirm if traffic was routed to fallback model variants or a smaller pool? customer reported 502s across both embeddings and generate.

ryan (oncall): yes — routing logs show fallback routes kicked in (we sent to smaller 1-GPU model) at 09:09 but capacity there hit saturation and queue grew. fallback reduced success rate further.

maria (customer): is this related to the billing retry at 08:55? we saw an automated email. could that have changed our capacity?

elena (billing): quick check — payment retry failed briefly but it didn't result in suspending org capacity. however, a minor rate-limiter threshold was briefly reapplied to API keys pending billing verification at 08:56 for 4 minutes — that led to some 429s upstream but shouldn't cause scaling failure. I'm going to open billing-789 to track.

ben (eng-runtime): reproducer for the timeout (run from a client):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"big-llm-v1","input":"a'*2000"}' -v
# response: HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
# body: {"error":"upstream timeout after 15000ms"}
```

ben (eng-runtime): server side we see this pattern: queue wait ~10–12s, then request forwarded to pod, then pod returns 3–4s later or fails if pod not ready. logs: \"pod init container wait=8.2s; model init=11.7s; handled=false\"

ashish (eng-sre): mitigation steps we've applied in the incident so far:
- patched ScaledObject: set minReplicaCount: 2, pollingInterval: 10, cooldownPeriod: 120 (applied at 09:18)
- patched HPA target CPU -> lower threshold for that deployment (applied 09:20)
- bumped readinessProbe initialDelaySeconds -> 12s (so kube doesn't consider pod failed while model is loading)
- enabled pre-warm init for model-pool (experimental flag fast-start=true) on 2 pods (applied 09:22)

deploy-bot: rollout started for model-pool-deploy @09:18 (deployment/model-pool-deploy: v98 -> v98+patch).

ryan (oncall): after the patches we saw scale to 4 replicas by 09:25 and error rate fell to <2%. Latency normalized by 09:27.

maria (customer): thanks — can you share what we should change on our side to avoid hitting this again? we want predictable p95 < 500ms for typical queries.

ben (eng-runtime): recommendations for customers to avoid user-visible timeouts on steep bursts:
- if steady baseline traffic is low, set a small dedicated minReplicaCount via dedicated capacity or request a smaller reserved pool for critical routes.
- for KEDA/HPA setups: set minReplicaCount>=1 for critical model groups, pollingInterval=10–15s, cooldownPeriod=120s.
- increase readinessProbe initialDelay to cover model load times (measure model load once and add margin).
- use lighter model variant for low-latency paths, with explicit routing in your client for latency-sensitive endpoints.
- use client-side timeouts shorter than gateway to allow retries with jitter.

ashish (eng-sre): internal followups and tickets: ENG-1234 (reduce KEDA polling defaults), ENG-1235 (detect metrics-server flakiness and fail open for KEDA), ENG-1236 (warmup pre-pull feature GA). I've added maria@example.com to the incident followup list.

elena (billing): billing-789 opened; I'll validate whether the short applied rate-limiter contributed to the initial surge to hosted fallback.

sarah (support): @maria — I'm going to book a 30-min postmortem with you and your SREs to walk the mitigation and recommended config changes. can we do today 16:00 UTC?

maria (customer): 16:00 UTC works. huge thanks — the fix helped and we've seen stabilized traffic. please include a reproducible runbook and the KEDA/HPA patch diff.

ben (eng-runtime): attaching quick patch diff we applied (sanitized):
```diff
- minReplicaCount: 0
- pollingInterval: 30
- cooldownPeriod: 300
+ minReplicaCount: 2
+ pollingInterval: 10
+ cooldownPeriod: 120
```

ashish (eng-sre): final notes: root cause = combination of (1) metrics-server/KEDA hiccup preventing timely scale trigger, (2) conservative scaledobject defaults and minReplica=0, (3) slow model cold-start times exacerbated by readinessProbe mismatch. Billing brief rate-limit noise may have added initial 429s which pushed traffic to fallback and increased load.

sarah (support): incident resolved, followups scheduled: ENG-1234, ENG-1235, ENG-1236, and a customer postmortem. closing thread but will keep updates in the ticket. :white_check_mark:
